text:
customer-joe: Hey team, hitting 401s only after bundling our app with esbuild + next.works. Native Node SDK works fine unbundled. Error: "Unauthorized: missing/invalid API key" from Redwood API. Happens in production builds, not dev.

customer-joe: Minimal repro: TS project, imports like `import {Redwood} from '@redwood/inference'` then bundle with esbuild (target: node, format: esm) and deploy to edge. Local unbundled `node dist/index.js` works.

customer-joe: package.json snippet:
```json
{
  "name": "client-app",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/inference": "^2.3.0"
  }
}
```

customer-joe: When bundled, requests hit our infra with Authorization header missing. Raw request before bundling: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...` After bundling it's absent. Any clues?

alex-support: thanks for the report — sorry about the outage. quick q: are you using the official npm package name exactly `@redwood/inference` or a forked build? also which bundler config (esbuild flags or next config)?

customer-joe: official package. esbuild cmd: `esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --outfile=dist/index.mjs` plus Next 14 edge runtime with an adapter. We left tree-shaking defaults.

devx-sam: common root cause: bundlers rewriting or removing Node built-ins or env usage that sets header at runtime. Is your API key read at build time (process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY) or injected at runtime? If it gets inlined as `undefined` at build time the runtime won't set it.

customer-joe: we read from env at runtime (process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY). Verified server runtime has env var. When I log `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` in the bundled file it prints the key. But outgoing fetch shows no header.

eng-lee: fyi, we had a reported issue where our v2.3 SDK uses conditional exports + dual entrypoints and some bundlers resolve to a shim that expects `globalThis.fetch` polyfill and rewrites our request helper. That shim accidentally drops headers when converting between Request/Headers in certain ESM->CJS interop cases. Does your bundle show any small helper module like `helpers/request-shim` inlined?

customer-joe: yes I can grep the bundle and I see a small helper chunk named `request-shim` with code that does `new globalThis.Request(url, opts)` and then does `fetch(req)` — header population happens earlier.

devx-sam: can you paste the top of that helper? small snippet enough.

customer-joe: snippet:
```js
function normalizeHeaders(h){
  if(!h) return new Headers();
  if(h instanceof Headers) return h;
  return new Headers(Object.entries(h));
}
// later
const req = new Request(url, { method, headers: normalizeHeaders(headers) });
```

customer-joe: It looks fine, but I notice `headers` ends up as an object with Symbol keys in the bundle for some reason (weird).

eng-lee: aha — bundler minification + exports map resolution pulled in a compiled CommonJS build path for one of our transitive deps that mutates header objects using `require()`-style helpers. When that interop runs in ESM it can put non-enumerable/symbol props on the headers object that `Object.entries` drops, causing Authorization to vanish.

alex-support: workaround: can you try changing normalizeHeaders to enumerate via `for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(headers || {}))` -> this still loses symbol keys. Better quick patch: prefer `new Headers(headers instanceof Headers ? headers : Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(headers || {}).map(k=>[k, headers[k]])))`. If that fixes it in your bundle we can confirm it's an interop hydration bug.

customer-joe: patched locally in node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/request-shim.mjs and rebundled — header now present and 200 responses. Good catch.

devx-sam: long-term fix: eng-sdk should make header normalization robust to non-enumerable keys and to CJS/ESM interop. Also ensure our package.json conditional exports avoid shipping a CommonJS alternative that bundlers accidentally prefer for ESM builds.

eng-lee: agree. We're going to patch the runtime to: 1) avoid Object.entries for header-like objects; 2) include an explicit import path for the ESM runtime in `exports` (`"./package.json": {..}`) and add tests for esbuild/next edge.

customer-joe: any guidance for consumers in the meantime? Is pinning to an older SDK safer?

alex-support: we'll publish a patched 2.3.1 with the header normalization fix. For now, either apply the local monkeypatch, or pin to 2.2.x where the reworked request-shim wasn't present (if you don't need features in 2.3). We'll add a blog note in the SDK changelog.

ci-bot: deploy status: created branch fix/esbuild-header-interop, CI queued.

eng-lee: assigning myself to the PR. Also adding a CHANGELOG entry about bundlers and conditional-exports. We'll follow up with a small migration note about `type`/`module` and how Next/Esbuild may choose different entrypoints.

customer-joe: thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround. saved our weekend. :raised_hands:

alex-support: closing the thread once 2.3.1 is published and you confirm production. keep us posted and ping if you hit any auth retry loops — 401s should not be retried by clients unless reauth succeeds.
